This type of sprout growth is commonly associated with decline of the root system where the tree attempts to regenerate foliage in response to canopy stress and loss of vascular function. Wounding was observed along the west buttress root crown area. Sounding tests produced highly resonant hollow tones indicating probable internal decay and hollow areas within the trunk base. These conditions are commonly observed in declining Southern Red Oaks exhibiting root loss, trunk decay, and advanced structural deterioration.
